The Federation of Free Worlds is a centralized technocracy established in 2550, following the construction of the first World Ship, the Apollyon.
Governed by the De Shars dynasty, the federation maintains control through four massive World Ships, encouraging the population to concentrate on them. 
Although nominally free, the federation enforces strict control and relocates inhabitants between the ships to strengthen the sense of belonging and loyalty, maintaining peace at the cost of individual freedom.

The Cosmo Kids are a pirate faction that emerged from the chaos and power struggles among the space corporations. 
Originally funded by corporations to disrupt competitors, they have grown into an independent and highly organized group. Comprised of defected warships, rogue miners, and adventurous rebels, the Cosmo Kids operate on the fringes of the Federation of Free Worlds. 
They raid trade routes, attack corporate assets, and provide an alternative way of life for those disillusioned with the federation's strict control. 
Their ultimate goal is to disrupt the federation's hold on power and carve out their own dominion in the cosmos.

ATTACK Select your ship and right-click on an enemy unit to attack. You can also initiate an attack by pressing the Attack button in the Command Panel or by using [ |-2-| ]. Hold [ |-1-| ] and drag the mouse to target multiple units at once. MOVE ATTACK Select your ship and press the Move Attack button in the Command Panel, or [ |-3-| ], to command it to move toward a position while attacking any enemies along the way. Ships behave in battle according to their assigned tactics and stances, which can be configured in the Tactics Panel. TACTICS Passive - The unit does not react to enemies at all. Defensive - The unit only reacts if it is attacked. Aggressive - The unit engages enemies within its intervention range or if allies are attacked nearby. Hunter - The unit actively seeks and attacks any visible enemy on the map. ATTACK STYLES Flyby - The unit performs repeated dive attacks, creating disruption and constant movement. Hold - The unit maintains its current position while attacking. Chase - The unit moves toward the target until it reaches firing range. Orbit - The unit circles around the enemy while attacking. Attacks can also be executed in formations, allowing for more coordinated and strategic strikes.

BUILD MODULES Open the Modules Panel, select the desired modules, and attach them to the Command Center, [ |-1-| ] to rotate. The Command Center expand by building structural modules, utility modules, facilities, and weapons. BUILD SHIPS Open the Ships Panel, select the facility from the top of the menu, if already built, or the Command Center, and choose the unit to produce. Ship types include fighters, mechguns, warships, and utilities. The Command Center build utility ships. Fighters and corvettes require Light Facilities, warships need Heavy Facilities.

DIRECTIONAL COMMANDS Move the camera left and right [ A ] [ D ] Move the camera forward and backward [ W ] [ S ] Move the camera up and down [ E ] [ Q ] You can also move the camera by moving the mouse cursor to the screen edges, if option is enabled. Hold [ |-1-| ] to set the arrival orientation, if needed. FOCUS Select an item/unit and press [ |-1-| ] to focus on it. Use the mouse wheel to zoom in and out.

CREW FULL Build additional Crew Quarters (Modules Panel) to increase max crew capacity. Make sure the Crew Quarters you've queued are actually under construction, check the build queues, and prioritize them if needed. The Crew button (Parameters panel) opens the detailed window (usage/capacity overview).

ENERGY CRISIS If systems consume more energy than is produced, build additional generators (Modules Panel). -Solar Panels: low output and storage. -Nuclear Generators: high output and storage. -Quantum Generators: very high output, no storage. -Power Accumulator: no output, very high storage. Generators placed close together gain a production boost. Overloaded generators take damage and may explode, causing area damage. Module energy usage is displayed in the Selection Panel (bottom-right) when selected; systems drawing energy can be disabled through the Command Panel. The Energy button (Parameters panel) opens the detailed window (income/outcome overview).

Resources are needed to build the base, create units, and unlock technologies. HARVEST Select Scavengers and right-click on asteroids to collect resources from them, or by pressing the Harvest button in the Command Panel, or [ |-1-| ]. Each asteroid type has its own yield and extraction speed. SALVAGE Select Scavengers and right-click on wrecks to salvage them or by using the Salvage button in the Command Panel, or [ |-2-| ]. Wrecks appear near derelicts or when ships are destroyed, they contain resources and technologies. REFINING Resources are returned to base for refining. Build Drop Points to speed it up.

Ships move across the map using propulsion or hyperspace. NAVIGATION Select a unit, right-click to open the movement interface, or by pressing the Move button in the Command Panel, or [ |-3-| ]. To move vertically, hold left-click and drag the mouse. Hold [ |-1-| ] and drag the mouse to set the arrival orientation. TACTICAL VIEW Press [ |-2-| ] to open the Tactical View, where all game overlays are enabled.

RESEARCH Open the Modules Panel, select the Research Center (under the Utility tab), and attach it to the Command Center. Once the Research Center is built, you can start researching available technologies from the Research Panel. Research is structured around Tech Eras, so you’ll need to reach a certain research level to unlock the next Tech Era. Click on Tech Era in the Parameters Panel to view details. TECHNOLOGY TREE The Technology Tree displays all available research paths. Here you can see the prerequisites needed to unlock the technologies you want to obtain.

RESOURCE CRISIS Balance harvesting, wreck salvaging, and refining. Build additional Scavengers (Ships Panel) or Drop Points (Modules Panel), if needed. Pause or slow down production queues for modules and ships. Salvage nearby wrecks for quick resources, assigned Scavengers will automatically keep the area clean. The Idle button in the Selection Panel selects inactive collectors. Command Center can enable Auto-Harvest (Command Panel): all collectors in range will automatically gather resources from nearby asteroids. The Resource button (Parameters panel) opens the detailed window (income/outcome overview).

RESOURCE FULL Build additional Resource Warehouses (Modules Panel) to increase max storage capacity. Enable Auto-Containers in the Deck Panel to auto-build and dock containers when storage is full. These can be recycled later. To offload resources, increase production queues or boost production speed.

TECH ERA Technological progress is represented by a level (Parameters Panel) and advances through Tech Eras: Era 1 - Start Era 2 - Level 100 Era 3 - Level 250 Era 4 - Level 500 Era 5 - Level 1000 Once a research threshold is reached, you can unlock the next Tech Era. To do so, open the Research Panel and, under the Utility section, start the corresponding research. Advancing to a new era consumes a significant amount of energy, but no resources. The Tech Era button (Parameters panel) opens the detailed window.

MODULES PANEL (left) Contains the list of modules that can be built along with the available research technologies. Both are organized into categories. PARAMETERS PANEL (top) Displays the main game parameters: resources, crew, energy, and the current technological era. SHIPS PANEL (right) Contains the types of ships that can be built, such as fighters, mechguns, warships, and utility ships. This panel also provides access to the docking bays of the Command Center and Facilities. SELECTION PANEL (bottom) Shows the current selection and its related statistics. It can display a single unit or multiple selections. This section also provides access to quick selection buttons, such as fleet, visible and armed ships. TACTICS PANEL (bottom-left) Contains all unit behaviors, stances and formations available to selected units. COMMANDS PANEL (bottom-right) Contains all commands that can be assigned to selected units.

AGGRESSIVE TACTIC [<color=#FF0000> |-1-| </color>]
Attacks all enemies that enter its range of action. Proactively engages in combat, seeking out and destroying enemies within its reach.

CHASE TARGET ATTACK
The unit advances towards the target until it is within firing range. Once in range, the unit maintains a constant distance between itself and the target. This style of attack is effective against slow-moving targets, as the unit can maintain a steady stream of fire.

CLAW FORMATION
This formation prioritizes protection of central units and counterattacks. Ideal for holding a position or defending against overwhelming force.
Enhances the unit's resistance and attack.

DEFENSIVE TACTIC [<color=#FF0000> |-1-| </color>]
Reacts if attacked directly or if allies within its range are attacked. Protects both itself and nearby allies, responding to any threats in its vicinity.

DELTA FORMATION
Units adopt a spread-out, mobile formation. This formation is suited for quick strikes, flanking maneuvers, and covering a wide area. Enhances the unit's resistance and attack.

LIGHT LEAD FORMATION
Lighter units like fighters and mechguns form the frontline, while heavier warships provide support from the rear. This formation prioritizes the mobility and firepower of light units for initial engagements, while the heavier warships offer sustained damage and protection.
Enhances the unit's resistance and attack.

FLYBY ATTACK
The unit approaches the target as closely as possible, firing its weapons, then veers away and repeats the attack. This attack style is used by fast, maneuverable units like fighters, allowing them to focus on specific targets and evade enemy fire.

FREE FORMATION STANCE
Units act independently, choosing their own targets and movement patterns, returning in formation when attack is completed. This formation style provides maximum flexibility and allows units to exploit individual strengths and opportunities.

HEAVY LEAD FORMATION
Heavier warships form the frontline, while lighter units like fighters and mechguns provide support from behind. This formation prioritizes the raw firepower and resilience of heavy warships for direct confrontation, while lighter units provide secondary support and harassment.
Enhances the unit's resistance and attack.

FRONTAL ATTACK
The unit aims its frontal weapons directly at the enemy. This attack style is used by warships with powerful forward-facing cannons, maximizing their offensive potential against head-on targets.

KEEP CLASS FORMATION STANCE
Units maintain formation and target selection based on their class type, grouping with similar units. This formation style promotes specialization and teamwork, allowing units to leverage their class-specific strengths in a coordinated manner.

KEEP FORMATION STANCE
Units strictly adhere to their assigned positions and targets, maintaining rigid formation. This formation style prioritizes discipline and concentrated firepower, maximizing the effectiveness of coordinated maneuvers.

HOLD POSITION ATTACK
The unit maintains its position, and continues firing at the target. This attack style is used by units equipped with turrets or long-range weapons, allowing them to sustain concentrated fire without compromising their position.

HUNTER TACTIC [<color=#FF0000> |-1-| </color>]
Attacks all enemies detected on the game map, within a wide range. Possesses exceptional awareness, capable of identifying and attacking enemies from a great distance.

BROADSIDE ATTACK
The unit positions itself sideways to the enemy, exposing its broadside and utilizing its longitudinal weapons. This attack style is used by warships with multiple turrets along their hull, allowing them to unleash a barrage of fire from different angles.

LEAVE FORMATION
Break up all ship formations.

ORBIT ATTACK
The unit circles around the enemy, attacking from the sides and rear. This attack style is used by mechguns, medium-speed vessels with versatile turrets, enabling them to flank and harass larger opponents.

PASSIVE TACTIC [<color=#FF0000> |-1-| </color>]
Does not respond to any enemy attacks. Remains stationary and takes no action, even when under enemy fire.

REACTIVE TACTIC [<color=#FF0000> |-1-| </color>]
Reacts only if attacked directly. Defends itself when targeted by enemies but does not actively seek out combat.

SCATTER FORMATION STANCE
Units maintain some degree of independence in movement but prioritize engaging the same target as the leader, returning in formation when attack is completed. This formation style balances flexibility with cohesion, allowing units to adapt to changing situations while maintaining a coordinated attack.

SPHERE FORMATION
Units form a circular, protective formation, prioritizing overall team resilience. This formation is designed to safeguard vulnerable units, such as support ships or carriers.
Enhances the unit's resistance and attack.

WALL FORMATION
Units form a tight wall. This formation is ideal for establishing a strong defensive position or overwhelming enemies with concentrated fire. Enhances the unit's resistance and attack.

Era One offers several game modes and is fully scalable to your preferred playstyle. You can choose fast, action‑packed matches or slow, strategic sessions where every move and resource matters. Gameplay settings determine both the pace and the duration of each match. The game speed setting increases resource gathering, construction, and research rates, creating different progression speeds for both you and your opponent. Training: A peaceful environment with all resource types and target dummies for testing weapons. Ideal for experimenting with construction and management features. Strongly recommended for new players for learning the core mechanics safely. Scenario: Maps of various sizes with enemies placed in pre‑built structures that control key areas. Resource-rich environments allow multiple strategies, while coordinated enemy attacks will eventually reach your base. Playable with all settings, supporting both tactical and aggressive playstyles. Deathmatch: A classic skirmish against a relentless AI that gathers resources, builds and manages its base, defends itself, and launches attacks whenever it has the strength to do so. Survival: Huge maps with limited, strategically placed resources. Progression is intentionally slow, requiring careful optimization and smart use of what you have. Stealth is essential: move freely but avoid detection. Enemies occupy the map with pre‑built structures and strike with targeted attacks. Tactical settings are forced. Enemy Waves: Arcade‑style combat with successive enemy waves, each stronger than the last. Survive the final assault to counterattack the enemy command center. A fast, intense mode suited for pure combat action, rewarding extra resources for every wave you defeat. War Machines: Face a sequence of enemy war machines entering a combat arena in progressive levels. Build and deploy your own war machine at the right moment. Win by keeping at least one command unit intact, earning extra resources after each victory. The match ends once the required number of wins has been reached. Resource Rush: Complete increasing objectives based on the amount of resources you must gather and store. This mode encourages efficient base setups and optimized logistics. Light enemy harassment creates pressure without overwhelming the player. Sandbox: Explore all Era One maps in a peaceful environment. Enemies may be present depending on the map, but they will not attack unless you choose to engage them, allowing full freedom in experimenting with layouts and strategies.
